source.title: AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus Document: Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure (2026)

findings: The consensus moves away from fixed LVEF cutoffs for phenotype classification while also describing the conventional HF with improved EF criterion of a 10-point LVEF increase to above 40%. The latter is retained as a trajectory description rather than treated as a universal phenotyping cutoff.
The proposed cause taxonomy is explicitly nonexhaustive and allows overlapping or evolving etiologic labels; overlapping examples were not forced into mutually exclusive categories.

The document states that a prior symptomatic HF diagnosis is generally retained permanently even when a patient reaches improvement, remission, or recovery. Recovery was therefore not interpreted as erasing the historical HF diagnosis.

schema_gaps: The recovered LiteratureAtom pattern has no dedicated expert_consensus_definition, consensus_classification, or consensus_recommendation atom kind. Consensus definitions and classifications are represented as atom_kind="other" and panel interpretations as author_conclusion.

Results from cited primary studies are secondary reports within this expert consensus document. They are tagged secondary_reported_result and are not represented as if this document generated primary participant data.
Conflict disclosure detail is represented at source-level rather than as one atom per disclosed company relationship.
extraction_limitations: The source is an expert consensus document, not a primary empirical study and not a clinical practice guideline.
The 71 cited publications were extracted as bibliography infrastructure and were not atomized.
The 26-page ESC national-reviewer disclosure supplement was used for conflict-of-interest context and was not atomized row by row.
All atoms remain needs_review because no human source-verification step is represented.
